issues.legal_issue: Statutorily recognized land-use privileges are property rights that cannot be curtailed by an executive order.
material_facts: The holder had recognized privileges to use adjacent waste land, including to collect forest produce and timber for agricultural and domestic purposes, subject to statutory rules.
An executive order reduced the holder’s entitlement to timber from land assigned to him, and the assignment imposed that restriction.
The restriction was not imposed by a law.
issues.conclusion: The land-use privileges were property rights, and the executive-order-based condition restricting the timber entitlement was invalid under Articles 19 and 31 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: The privileges, though described as such, were recognized by the Madras Forest Rules framed under Section 26 of the Madras Forest Act and by the relevant Standing Orders. Rule 7(A) regulated their exercise, including the use of forest produce for agricultural or domestic purposes and the Collector’s authority to determine what those purposes included. The rights could be curtailed, abridged, or taken away only by law, not by executive fiat; the executive order and resulting condition violated Articles 19 and 31 of the Constitution.

rule.if: constitutional_property_claim and recognized_land_use_rights and executive_order_reduced_rights and no_law_authorized_reduction

predicates.constitutional_property_claim: A person challenged a restriction on recognized land-use rights as an unconstitutional deprivation of property.
predicates.recognized_land_use_rights: The person held legally recognized privileges to use land or its produce, subject to prescribed conditions.
predicates.executive_order_reduced_rights: The government reduced those privileges through an executive order.
predicates.no_law_authorized_reduction: No law authorized the reduction imposed by the government.

issues.definition: When a constitutional property claim concerns legally recognized land-use rights reduced by executive order without authorization by law, the restriction is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: An illegal condition attached to an assignment may be severed while the valid assignment remains in force if the condition is separable and its removal leaves the assignment effective.
material_facts: The assignment of land to a person entitled to preferential consideration included an invalid condition restricting the timber entitlement.
The condition was not an integral part of the assignment, and deleting it left the assignment effective and complete.
The challenge in the writ proceeding was directed at the condition.
issues.conclusion: The invalid condition could be quashed without quashing the assignment; the assignment remained valid without that condition.
issues.legal_principle: The appropriate relief depends on the circumstances, including whether the valid and invalid parts of an order are severable and whether the remainder remains viable and self-contained. The Court relied on Mahaboob Sheriff v. Mysore State Transport Authority, where the illegal part of an order was severed and quashed while the lawful remainder stood. It held that R. M. D. Chamarbaugwalla v. Union of India was not in point.

rule.if: assignment_challenged_in_writ_proceeding and illegal_condition_attached and condition_severable and remaining_assignment_effective

predicates.assignment_challenged_in_writ_proceeding: A person challenged an assignment in a writ proceeding.
predicates.illegal_condition_attached: The assignment included a condition that was unlawful.
predicates.condition_severable: The unlawful condition could be removed without making the rest of the assignment truncated or ineffective.
predicates.remaining_assignment_effective: The assignment remained viable and complete after removal of the unlawful condition.

issues.definition: When an assignment challenged in a writ proceeding contains an unlawful condition that can be removed without impairing the effective remainder, the assignment remains valid without that condition.

issues.legal_issue: The applicability of asserted general land-grant rules to a special land assignment is not established when the party asserting their applicability does not produce the rules.
material_facts: The government asserted that general land-grant rules governed the assignment.
The government did not provide a copy of those rules, explaining that it had been unable to obtain one despite efforts.
The lower court had found that the assignment was not governed by those rules.
issues.conclusion: The Court was unable to hold that the lower court’s finding was incorrect.
issues.legal_principle: Without the text of the rules said to govern the assignment, the Court could not conclude that the lower court’s finding about their applicability was wrong.

predicates.special_land_assignment_dispute: The dispute concerns whether general land-grant rules govern a particular kind of land assignment.
predicates.party_asserting_general_grant_rules_fail: The party claiming that the general rules apply does not produce their text.

issues.definition: When a special land-assignment dispute turns on the applicability of asserted general rules and the asserting party does not produce those rules, their applicability is not established.
